doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Joining the Messengers and moving to New York
title: Rock Island, Art Blakey at the Stage Door and the Cotton Club
summary: After a couple of months, Ware gigs out of town, sits in with Blakey and Ira Sullivan, and hangs at the Cotton Club while Miles is in town.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Well, how long did you keep that gig there?
I stayed there maybe a couple of months.

Then I went out of town with Leo. We went down to Rock Island for a week -- one of them little joints down there. And I came back in town, and I had a gig with Ira Sullivan Art Solomon, somewhere -- I forgot where, and he said, Blakey "Well, man, Art Baker just come back in town." So I said, "Well, I got to catch that band, you know."

So we go out the Stage Door -- a place called the Stage Door Lounge; 63rd and Blackistone. These were all nightclubs, and I had a chance to listen to the great Lou Buhaina Ayman -- that was a beautiful man.

Oh yeah, for a long time, but he was Buhaina you know, he was still Art Blakey; that was his Muslim name. I think the band all gave their notice, I'm not sure. Anyway, he asked Ira and I to come up and sit in, and we did -- so he taught us our names for future reference, and not long after that, I'm hanging out -- Ira and I went down to Hannibal, and Wilbur Campbell and Eddie Baker Missouri, and play a little weekend gig, and when I come back, we were all hanging out around the Cotton Club -- that was the swinging joint -- something like the Flame used to be -- a Monday morning, Monday night all day jam session, you know? And it was run by 2 musicians -- Bobby Paine, and I forgot the other pianist.
And it was something like a [clan] house of musicians. See, I didn't have no permanent address then; I was still chasing that powder, like a fool, but that was my lifestyle, and I'll

never forget, Miles was in town -- he was working around the corner at a club called [The Crown Phillip.] Billy Joe Powell, and that was the first time I had ever met Powell up close. I had heard about him in Detroit, but he was with Miles -- and Trane was with him, and Philly Red didn't come in town with him for some reason. Billy Joe was with him, and they used Billy Greene, a Chicago pianist, and he worked with them.
